Beta 3: artist pictures reach the iPod even when there is nothing new to send, Preferences explains what PodBox and its People folder are, a band whose name has no letters (such as "@") gets an artist page, and adding a cover to an album no longer leaves a stray "track" behind. Beta 2 brought devices and artists. Sending to a device now looks at what is already there, copies only what is missing and asks once about albums that differ. PodBox iPods are recognised, get artist pictures and stop filling up with hidden Mac files. And every artist gets a page in the inspector: a portrait, who they are, a short bio and what your library holds of them, filled in quietly in the background and yours to edit. Beta 1 brought shell materials, the cover screen and the Pocket theme. 2.3.3 went out only as a release candidate, so everything listed under 2.3.3 below is new to stable users too. Betas are offered only to people who turned on Receive beta updates.
### Added
- **Pocket, a fourth built-in theme.** Handheld grey by day and console purple by night, with a moulded plastic shell, a grey LCD and its own logo. In the compact player and the mini player the album art sits in a pixel screen set into the case. - **Shell materials.** The Theme Editor's SHELL MATERIAL section offers Moulded Plastic, Brushed Metal, Bead-Blasted Metal and Carbon Weave beside Texture Grain, each with its own strength. A theme wears one at a time, and the mini player's glass wears it too. - **Cover screen.** The Theme Editor's COVER SCREEN section turns the album art in the compact player and the mini player into an LCD: LCD Grid lays a fine grid over the sharp picture, Pixel LCD redraws it in big square pixels, and Handheld LCD adds the soft colours of an old handheld screen. PIXEL SIZE picks how big the pixels are. A track with no art shows an unlit screen. The full player, the gallery and the inspector keep the plain picture. - **Sending to a device looks at what is already there.** Before anything is written, CrateDigger compares the albums you are sending with the device. Tracks it already has are skipped, missing tracks of a partly copied album are filled in beside the rest of it, and new albums go over as usual. This is the same for copy devices, converting devices and the offline queue with SYNC, and an MP3 you replace with a FLAC is recognised as the same track, not copied in beside it. - **An "Already on" sheet for albums that differ.** When an album on the device is a different quality, has different cover art or is another release of the same name, one sheet lists them side by side with what would be sent. Choose Replace, Keep both or Leave it for each album, or set them all at once. Nothing is chosen for you, and Cancel sends nothing. Albums you leave alone stop coming back; the sheet can show them again, and Preferences > Devices can forget them all. - **Folder Art is a switch.** Preferences > Devices has a Folder Art option for each device, and the Convert panel has a Folder Art row, so a cover.jpg beside the tracks can be combined with keeping, re-embedding or stripping the art inside the files. Rockbox iPods keep their old default (cover.jpg on, art inside the files stripped). Each device also remembers its own art setting. Ordinary conversions have the switch too, off by default. - The Devices screen's Artwork cell says when a cover.jpg is written as well as art inside the files. - **PodBox iPods are recognised.** When a device runs the PodBox firmware, Preferences > Devices shows which one (model, build and library layout), the Devices screen calls it a PodBox, and CrateDigger tells you what the iPod will make of your music: Mac files it reads as broken tracks, artist pictures switched off, a music folder it does not scan, the play log off, names it cannot match, paths that are too long, and compilations without an album artist. It only reads the iPod when it is plugged in. - **A folder layout PodBox reads well.** "PodBox recommended" names folders Artist / 2010 Album, which is how PodBox sorts albums, and leaves the year out for an album that has none. It is picked in Preferences > Devices for a new iPod profile; a layout you already use is never changed. - **Clean Up Mac Files.** Right-click a device or one of its folders, or use Preferences > Devices, to remove the hidden `._` files macOS leaves on an iPod's disk. Only files that are provably macOS metadata for a music, picture or playlist file are removed, a copy of each is kept on your Mac, and nothing happens until you confirm the count. A switch can also tidy the folders a transfer just wrote into; it is off until you turn it on. - **Next steps and Eject after a transfer.** The summary says what to do on the iPod (for PodBox: Update Database, Update Art Cache) and has an Eject key. The Devices screen reminds you to update the art cache until the iPod has. - **Artist pictures for PodBox.** The Artist Pictures sheet shows the artists on your iPod and writes a small square picture for those the iPod has none for, either in its Artwork/People folder or as folder.jpg in each artist's folder. Pictures come from your own files, an artist.jpg in your library, Deezer, or Wikimedia Commons (found through MusicBrainz), and are taken without asking only when your albums confirm the artist; anything unsure waits for your pick. Only the artist's name is sent. A picture you already have on the iPod is never replaced, and the ones CrateDigger added can be removed. Pictures after a transfer wait until you mark the check passed for that iPod. - **Artist pages.** Select an artist (or choose Show Artist on a track) and the inspector shows who they are: a portrait, where they are from, their years, members and genres, the opening of their Wikipedia article (with its credit and a link), and what your library holds of them, from albums and formats to plays and the tracks you play most. When two acts share a name, the page asks which one you mean instead of guessing. - **Artist info fills itself in.** A quiet background lookup finds each artist on MusicBrainz, Wikidata, Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons and Deezer, one at a time and the one you are looking at first. It never slows a FIX TAGS or artwork search you started, and it pauses while you scan, convert or copy to a device, when CrateDigger is hidden, on Low Power and offline. Only artist names are sent. Settings > Integrations > Look up artist info and photos turns it off; Look Up Again on an artist page still works. - **Edit an artist and their photos.** Edit Artist lets you correct any fact (what you type always wins over what was looked up), paste the right MusicBrainz artist, add as many photos as you like, and choose the one shown. The artist photo viewer pages through them, makes one the default, and shows where each came from. - **Artists whose name has no letters get a page.** A band called "@" or "!!!" now has an artist page, photos and edits of its own. They are not looked up automatically, since a search for "@" finds other acts.
### Changed
- **Preferences explains PodBox.** The iPod's section in Preferences > Devices is now called PodBox and says what it is, what "In /Artwork/People" means (one portrait per artist in the iPod's own People folder, named after the artist, which PodBox looks at first), what "In artist folders" writes, and what Verified on this iPod unlocks. - **Artist Pictures says why some artists can't have one.** PodBox cannot show a picture for a name with no letters or digits, wherever the file is, and the sheet now says so instead of a vague "cannot be named". - **The iPod shows the artist's own photo.** The picture CrateDigger writes for an artist on a PodBox iPod is now the default photo on their artist page, so the two always agree. Picking a picture in Artist Pictures makes it the artist's photo too, and No Picture is now Don't Send to iPod, which keeps the photo in CrateDigger. A photo found for an artist CrateDigger is not sure of waits for you to pick it before it can reach the iPod. Pictures you had already chosen carry over the first time you open your library. - **MusicBrainz lookups share one speed limit.** Artwork search, FIX TAGS, DEEP SCAN, CD lookup and artist pictures wait their turn at the same gate instead of each keeping its own count, so using two together no longer gets refused by MusicBrainz. - **Carbon wears carbon weave** in place of its grain, and its selection lamp in the light theme now glows the same orange as the light it throws on the row. - **Llama '97 wears brushed metal.** - Themes you made that inherit from Carbon pick up the weave with it, even one that sets its own grain. To keep grain, open the theme in the Theme Editor, switch Texture Grain on and save.
### Fixed
- **Artist pictures go to the iPod even when nothing else needs sending.** Sending albums the iPod already has stopped at "Nothing to transfer" before the pictures, so an iPod with pictures switched on could go without any. They are now written then, and the message says how many. - **Adding a cover to an album no longer leaves a stray track.** Embedding the cover into each file used a temporary file named like a song beside it; quitting while that was still running left an empty one, which CrateDigger and PodBox both listed as a track by Unknown Artist. The temporary file is now hidden and named so nothing reads it as music, quitting waits for the covers to finish, and a track that could not be updated is named in a message instead of silently keeping its old art. - **Device transfers no longer leave half-written files.** Each file is written under a temporary name and moved into place when it is complete, so a failed or cancelled send keeps the old file, and an unplugged drive does not leave a track that stops halfway. - **Replacing an album never leaves it empty.** The new files are written first and the old ones removed only when every new file arrived. Cancel keeps the old files. - **Nothing is written or removed outside the device's music folder**, so backups and an iPod's own database are left alone. - **The device's contents stay up to date after a send.** The browser and the offline queue see what was just copied, replaced or removed without a rescan. Copy-mode devices no longer silently write "(2)" copies, and SYNC no longer converts a file more than once. - Cancel and the busy light now follow a device send, SYNC or conversion all the way to the end, including the final renames, deletions and cover files. - **Sending to a device no longer leaves hidden Mac files behind.** Files are copied without the extra information macOS adds on a FAT disk, which is what made `._` files that PodBox read as broken tracks, and the one `._` file macOS still makes for each file and folder CrateDigger writes (to hold a tag it cannot drop) is removed straight after. Converting devices convert on your Mac and copy the finished file over, so nothing is written to the device half-done. - **Every write to a device is checked first.** CrateDigger now writes to a device only in the places it is meant to (the music folder, covers beside it, artist pictures), never in the player's own folders, and replaces or removes only files it can show it wrote itself or that you chose to replace. A file you added is left alone and reported. A copy of anything replaced or removed is kept on your Mac. - **Names a FAT disk cannot hold are fixed on the way.** Folders and files with characters such as ? : or a trailing dot (R.E.M.) are written with the characters removed or replaced, so the album lands instead of failing.
